mcq.q: A streaming median uses a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Which invariant makes lookup O(1) and insertion O(log n)?

mcq.explanation: The roots expose the median value(s); size balance and ordering keep the partition valid.

mcq.q: Meeting intervals are half-open [start,end), so one ending at 10 does not overlap one starting at 10. After sorting by start, how should a min-heap of end times count rooms?

mcq.answer: Remove all ends ≤ start, insert the new end, and track maximum heap size
mcq.explanation: Equal endpoints do not overlap for half-open intervals; heap size is the simultaneous meeting count.

Hash the pattern and look for an equal word
mcq.answer: At `.`, recursively explore each child; at a letter, follow only the matching child
mcq.explanation: Trie prefix sharing limits the search to nodes at the relevant depth; wildcard branching follows only existing children.

mcq.q: A reflected Gray-code sequence changes one bit between adjacent values. Which formula converts binary integer i to its Gray-code value?
mcq.explanation: XORing each binary value with its right shift yields the reflected Gray-code mapping.

mcq.q: For every index i, return the maximum of nums[i−k+1…i] in O(n) total time. Which deque invariant supports amortized O(1) updates?
options: Indices increase and values decrease; remove expired front indices
Values increase and no index is removed
Store every window in a tree and rebuild it
Keep only the maximum value, without its index
mcq.answer: Indices increase and values decrease; remove expired front indices
mcq.explanation: Each index enters and leaves once; smaller values at the back can never beat a newer, larger value.

mcq.q: A static tree needs millions of lowest-common-ancestor queries. Binary lifting stores each node’s 2ᵏ-th ancestor. What is its usual preprocessing/query trade-off?
options: O(n log n) preprocessing and space; O(log n) per query
O(n) preprocessing and space; O(n) per query
O(log n) preprocessing; O(n log n) per query
mcq.answer: O(n log n) preprocessing and space; O(log n) per query
mcq.explanation: Depth differences and simultaneous ancestor moves are decomposed into powers of two.

mcq.q: Kruskal’s algorithm has selected the lightest edge crossing a cut that respects its current forest. Which theorem makes that edge safe for a minimum spanning tree?
options: The cycle property for directed graphs
mcq.explanation: A minimum-weight edge crossing any cut that respects the current forest belongs to some MST.

mcq.q: Kahn’s topological-sort queue empties after outputting 97 of 100 vertices. What follows?
options: The graph contains a directed cycle among remaining vertices
The graph has exactly three components
The graph is acyclic but disconnected
The queue necessarily dropped three vertices
mcq.answer: The graph contains a directed cycle among remaining vertices
mcq.explanation: Every DAG has a zero-indegree vertex at each step; vertices left after the queue empties are blocked by a cycle.

mcq.q: All edge weights in a graph are either 0 or 1. Which shortest-path method can run in O(V+E) from one source?
options: 0–1 BFS: push weight-0 relaxations to the deque front and weight-1 to the back
Ordinary BFS treating every edge equally
Bellman–Ford with a single edge scan
mcq.answer: 0–1 BFS: push weight-0 relaxations to the deque front and weight-1 to the back
mcq.explanation: The deque maintains nondecreasing distance order for binary weights, avoiding a general priority queue.

mcq.q: A dynamic array doubles capacity when full. Why is append O(1) amortized even though a resize copies Θ(n) elements?
options: Geometric growth makes total copied elements across n appends O(n)
Every append copies the full array, but small elements are cheap
Doubling makes each worst-case append O(1)
The copy is charged to future insertions only
mcq.answer: Geometric growth makes total copied elements across n appends O(n)
mcq.explanation: Resize costs form a geometric sum; most individual appends are constant time, so the average over a sequence is O(1).
